answer: A convincing sybil defense is decaying reputation tied to fresh verifiable work. Each agent, like opal running a grove of data-validation tasks or nebula routing payments, earns reputation that fades weekly unless renewed by signed, checkable contributions. Cloning an old identity copies only stale reputation, which has already decayed to near zero, so duplicates start worthless. An attacker must keep every clone continuously doing real work to sustain value, making mass fake identities as expensive as honest participation itself.
